text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.

- Severo de Almeida, president of the Tax Workers' Union, said the government exercised no controls over those who failed to submit tax returns. People who do not submit tax returns are not penalised, he said.
- New direct foreign investment projects in Portugal total some 200 billion escudos, mostly automotive industry investment, government calculations show.
- Antonio Mega Ferreira, one of the directors of Expo 1998, unveiled details of the cultural programme of the exhibition, including a show entitled "A dive into the future".
- The government will reorganise the civil service to bring those employed on "precarious" terms in line with those who have formal employment contracts.

- The number of patients with tuberculosis has fallen by 35 percent in the last decade, although the incidence of the disease in Portugal is the highest in Europe with 49.6 cases per 100,000 inhabitants.
- Annual deficit of the Health Ministry rose by 61.9 percent in 1996 compared with 1995 as revenues fell short of expectations.

- Eurostat is expected to end its analysis this week into statistical formulae used by the Portuguese government to account for the costs of the construction of the "Vasco da Gama" bridge over the River Tagus, as well as state guarantees for exports.

- The privatisation process involving Portuguese utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal will include a presentation to international financial analysts in Lisbon on April 7. On May 19 the privatisation will take place in a special session at Lisbon bourse, according to government sources.
